title: acs step result (runs/<run-id>/steps/<skill>/result.json)
description: The document a step writes when it ends, and the post-hook's input -- previously validated ad hoc by `acs phase validate`. `acs step finish` reads the step's transition out of this file, which is why it is a schema rather than a convention. For `code` it also carries `since_sha` and the `resolutions[]` that answer every confirmed finding of the previous verdict by id (§2.3).

skill.description: Optional. The kernel knows which skill wrote this from WHERE the file is (steps/<skill>/result.json), so a document that repeats it is ceremony -- and a check of the document's substance should not fail on identity the caller already supplied on the command line.

run_id.description: Optional, for the same reason as `skill`: the run is the partition this file sits in.

outcome.description: Checked against the skill's own vocabulary, not enumerated here.

no_op.description: True when the pre-hook completed this step without spawning a coordinator, because the plan's ## Contract block said nothing was owed.

tokens.description: Legacy: accepted so an older coordinator's result still validates, and ignored -- acs records no usage (ADR-0103, ADR-0104).

cost_usd.description: Legacy: accepted so an older coordinator's result still validates, and ignored -- acs records no usage (ADR-0103, ADR-0104).

cost_basis.description: Legacy: accepted so an older coordinator's result still validates, and ignored -- acs records no usage (ADR-0103, ADR-0104).

role_usage.description: Legacy: accepted so an older coordinator's result still validates, and ignored -- acs records no usage (ADR-0103, ADR-0104).

model_usage.description: Legacy: accepted so an older coordinator's result still validates, and ignored -- acs records no usage (ADR-0103, ADR-0104).

api_duration_ms.description: Legacy: accepted so an older coordinator's result still validates, and ignored -- acs records no usage (ADR-0103, ADR-0104).

since_sha.description: code only: the base the review diffs from, copied from the verdict it answered.

resolutions.description: code only: every confirmed finding of the previous verdict, answered by id. There is no third option -- a finding is fixed or disputed.

reason.description: Required on `disputed`: the evidence that defeats the claim. The next adjudicator receives it and rules again -- a dispute is not a way out.
